links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading level of LLM-generated patient education materials without reading-level specification
links.effect: Unspecified-prompt LLM handouts averaged FKRL 9.8-11.45 for common and rare conditions, above the 7th-8th grade US average; AAD PEMs averaged 9.35 and 9.50.
links.quote: Without specification, all LLMs consistently generate handouts above the average US reading level.

links.outcome: Proportion of handouts meeting target reading level when prompted with specified grade level
links.effect: Specifying fifth/seventh-grade FKRL lowered FKRL to 4.22-7.43 and 5.98-7.28; GPT-4 met the fifth-grade level in 86% (69/80) of iterations, though DermGPT met it in only 5% (4/80).
links.quote: With prompting, LLMs consistently produce PEMs at lower reading levels than AAD PEMs for the same conditions and may be a useful supplementary tool in sharing appropriately readable dermatologic information with patients.

links.outcome: Citation validity in LLM-generated patient education handouts, per resident reviewers
links.effect: Reviewers found blank or misaligned references (e.g., psoriasis PEM citing acne literature), and some cited references were untraceable.
links.quote: Some references cited by LLMs were also found to be untraceable after a thorough literature search.

links.outcome: Ability of LLMs to produce materials at low literacy target levels (fifth grade)
links.effect: Fifth-grade compliance varied by model: GPT-4 90% common/82% rare, ChatGPT-3.5 57%/50%, DocsGPT 42%/52%, DermGPT 0%/10%.
links.quote: At the fifth-grade reading level, GPT-4 was better at producing PEMs for both common and rare conditions than ChatGPT-3.5 (P=.001 and P=.01, respectively), DermGPT (P<.001 and P=.03, respectively), and DocsGPT (P<.001 and P=.02, respectively).

unlisted_practices: Specifying a target Flesch-Kincaid reading level in the LLM prompt to control readability of patient education materials
Human health literacy team review of patient education materials

links.effect: At/below target FKRL: ChatGPT-3.5 53% fifth/65% seventh; GPT-4 86%/45%; DocsGPT 48%/75%; DermGPT 5%/40%.
links.quote: ChatGPT-3.5 created materials at or below the specified fifth- or seventh-grade FKRL in 53% (43/80) and 65% (52/80) of iterations, respectively; GPT-4 created materials at or below the fifth- or seventh-grade FKRL in 86% (69/80) and 45% (36/80) of iterations, respectively; DocsGPT created materials at or below the specified fifth- or seventh-grade FKRL in 48% (38/80) and 75% (60/80) of iterations, respectively; and DermGPT created materials at or below the specified fifth- or seventh-grade FKRL in 5% (4/80) and 40% (32/80) of iterations, respectively ( Tables 2 - 4 ).

links.effect: Most documents required prior medical knowledge; many medical terms were not defined within handouts.
links.quote: Most documents’ content was found to require prior medical knowledge to sufficiently comprehend, as many medical terms were frequently not defined within the handout.

links.effect: Some LLM-cited references were untraceable; other references were often blank or misaligned with the PEM purpose.
links.quote: Some references cited by LLMs were also found to be untraceable after a thorough literature search.

links.outcome: combined readability, understandability, and accuracy score
links.effect: Common-condition scores ranged from 13/15 (87%) for GPT-4 to 14.75/15 (98%) for DermGPT.
links.quote: Results from the preservation of meaning analysis revealed that for common conditions, handouts generated by DermGPT ranked the highest for overall ease of reading, patient understandability, and accuracy (14.75/15, 98%), followed by DocsGPT (14.25/15, 95%), ChatGPT-3.5 (13.5/15, 90%), and GPT-4 (13/15, 87%).

links.outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient education materials
links.effect: Without specifying reading level, LLM-generated PEMs had average FKRLs of 9.8-11.21 for common and 9.85-11.45 for rare conditions, exceeding the average US reading level of seventh to eighth grade.
links.quote: Without specification, all LLMs consistently generate handouts above the average US reading level.
